items.headline: U.S. Stocks Conclude Record-Setting Week with Broad Gains
items.summary: U.S. equities finished Friday's trading session higher, marking a positive close to a record-setting week. The market demonstrated resilience, rallying into the upcoming earnings season despite persistent inflation concerns and the Federal Reserve's signals on future rate hikes. Technology stocks rebounded after Thursday's sell-off, contributing to the overall upbeat sentiment.

items.headline: Humana Surges on Medicare Advantage Rating
items.summary: Humana ($HUM) jumped 13% today after improving its Medicare Advantage rating and receiving an analyst upgrade. Oppenheimer raised its price target for Humana to $475 from $405.

items.headline: Veea Climbs on Nasdaq Compliance
items.summary: Veea ($VEEA) soared 66.93% after announcing it had regained full compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing requirements.

items.headline: Darkiris Inc. Plunges
items.summary: Darkiris Inc. ($DKI) experienced a significant decline, dropping over 51% today.

items.headline: Delta Air Lines Falls on Disappointing Earnings
items.summary: Delta Air Lines ($DAL) shares slipped after the company reported third-quarter adjusted earnings and revenue that fell below market expectations, leading to a cut in its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Real Estate and Healthcare Lead, Communication Services Lags
items.summary: Real Estate (+1.85%) and Healthcare (+1.48%) emerged as the dominant sectors within the S&P 500 today, demonstrating strong performance. In contrast, Communication Services (-1.62%) was among the weakest performers. Energy also showed positive gains, while technology stocks rebounded after earlier weakness this week.

items.headline: Fed Minutes Signal Further Rate Hikes Possible
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, released Wednesday, indicated that most Federal Reserve officials anticipate another interest rate increase may be necessary this year to combat inflation. However, policymakers may opt to hold rates steady during their October meeting.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Dips in October
items.summary: The University of Michigan's preliminary Consumer Sentiment Index for October fell to 46.3, missing economists' forecasts and indicating a continued decline in consumer confidence. This comes as rising prices continue to weigh on households.

items.headline: EU and China Strike Interim Trade Deal; Trump Comments on Iran
items.summary: Trade envoys from the European Union and China reached a broad initial deal today aimed at de-escalating trade tensions, which could include lower tariffs for some European goods to China and measures to stabilize rare earth supply chains. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump stated on Thursday that the U.S. would not launch strikes against Iran before the upcoming midterm elections, a comment that could ease some geopolitical uncertainty.
